items.author: Ben (2026-09-10); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: A rolled world cannot be judged, because round 4 never shows whether the arc happened in it
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-10, the second half of the randomise ruling: rolling should give "the player the ability to see if their world will contain these types of structures". Ben placed this IN sprint 38 (elicitation, "in-sprint-38").

RANDOMNESS WITHOUT A READOUT IS NOT A CHOICE. BL-890 makes each arrival a fresh world; this item is what lets the player tell one from another. Without it a reroll is a blind redraw -- the player cannot see whether this world produced an empire, a collapse, or five polities that never fought, so "reroll until it looks interesting" is not actually available to them.

THE STRUCTURES ARE THE ONES GENERATION_STRATEGY.md sec The asymmetry is POLITICAL names: were polities eliminated, did an empire form, did it fall, are the survivors unequal. history_sweep already computes every one of these per world (eliminations, top/peak share, BL-767 rise/peak/fall) -- the quantities exist and are simply not surfaced.

RELATED SURFACES ALREADY DESIGNED: BL-817 (history playback record) and BL-830 (top-sixteen scoreboard) are round 4's instrument. Check what they now cover before adding a surface -- this may be a read on those rather than a new panel. SCOPE THAT FIRST.

DONE WHEN: after round 4 the player can see, without leaving the wizard, whether this world's history contains the arc -- and can reroll on that basis.

=== CAPTURE-VERIFIED 2026-09-11; STILL PARTIAL, AND THE REASON IS NOT COSMETIC. ===

WHAT IS PROVEN. The arc readout renders off today's build and is legible. Headless capture `press_04_round5_history.png` shows, under a "What happened here" rule: "56 polities, 0 destroyed. / The largest empire held 8% of the world; 2 rose and fell back. / At the end the greatest holds 8%, the least 1 region." That is exactly the structure GENERATION_STRATEGY.md sec The asymmetry is POLITICAL names -- eliminations, whether an empire formed, whether it fell, how unequal the survivors are -- in a form a player can read without watching the replay. The item's SUBSTANCE is delivered.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN, AND IT IS THE HALF THIS ITEM IS ABOUT. The player must be able to REACH the round and reroll on what they see. `history_lapse_press.lua` walks the wizard with real presses and went RED here: four assertions fail, every Next after round 3 misses, and the wizard never leaves round 3 (0-based 2). A purpose-written probe (`scripts/verify/round4_arc_reach.lua`) pressed the column at y = 995, 1005, 1017, 1027, 1040, 1055 and 1070 and NONE advanced the round.

THE LIKELY CAUSE, STATED AS A HYPOTHESIS RATHER THAN A FINDING. Round 3 carries a preference block (Drawdown) that the pass rounds do not, and this item then added three more lines above the footer. The footer follows the column's content, so the Next control appears to sit at or below the bottom edge at this window size -- a surface that grew until it pushed its own exit off the screen. The capture shows a blue footer bar clipped at the very bottom of the panel.

TWO REASONS THIS IS NOT YET CALLED A REGRESSION. (1) The verify window reports "window 1720x1080" while the capture is 1920x1080, so capture pixels and click coordinates may not be the same space, and the probe's misses could be a coordinate-space error rather than an unreachable control. (2) The wizard's left column has a scrollbar, so a human may simply scroll to the footer -- and the verify API has NO scroll verb for that column (`scroll_panel` knows only named ledger windows), so a script cannot test the human path.

WHY IT WAS NOT LIVE-CLICKED. Ben was using the PC (2026-09-11) and asked for captures instead. Worth recording: computer-use resolved "ProjectIo" to `.claude/worktrees/elated-mclean-7dd61c/build/ProjectIo.exe`, a TWO-DAY-OLD binary, while the real build sat at `build/ProjectIo.exe` -- so a live check taken without checking that path would have verified the wrong exe and looked fine doing it.

WHAT REMAINS: establish whether round 3's Next is reachable by a human at 1080p. If it is not, that is a blocker on the whole wizard and not merely on this readout. BL-904 owns the reachability question and the missing scroll verb.
items.resolution:
CODE LANDED 2026-09-11 (fcf118e2). LIVE CHECK OWED -- hence partial, per the standing rule that a UI requirement needs a click and not only a clean compile.

A PURE READ over era_timelapse's existing polity samples. No new field, nothing on the save seam -- which is what the item asked to be checked first, and the answer was that the record already carries everything: population, regions held and capacities per polity per recorded step.

WHAT IT ANSWERS, and it is a different question from the scoreboard beside it. The scoreboard shows who leads RIGHT NOW and re-ranks as the centuries pass. This says whether anything HAPPENED: how many polities, how many were destroyed, the largest empire ever formed, how many rose and fell back, and how unequal the survivors are. That is the question a player rolling a world actually asks, and without it BL-890's reroll is a blind redraw.

EVERY DEFINITION IS history_sweep's OWN, deliberately -- ROSE is a peak at least double the start and at least three regions more, FELL is ending at or under 60% of that peak -- so the panel and the harness cannot drift into describing the same world differently.

A QUIET AGE GETS ITS OWN SENTENCE rather than a row of zeroes, because Ben ruled on 2026-09-10 that a seed refusing war is a legitimate outcome, and a readout that renders it as failure would contradict that.

OWED: open the built app, reach round 4, confirm the panel renders and reads correctly against a world whose arc is known from the sweep.

items.author: Claude (found building BL-899); Ben to confirm priority
items.title: A culture that crossed water to get where it is cannot be told from one that walked
items.design:
FOUND WHILE BUILDING BL-899 (seafaring creed), 2026-09-11. Ben settled that sea legs are earned from THREE upstream facts: a coastal cradle, A CROSSING IN ITS MIGRATION, and a sea or storm god in the pantheon. Only two of the three survive into `creed_state`, so BL-899 shipped deriving `culture::sea_legs_q` from those two and documented the gap at the field.

WHAT IS MISSING, EXACTLY. `colonisation.cpp`'s crude overseas hop KNOWS it coined a daughter on the far side of water -- the fact exists at the moment of spawning. But `culture_spawn` carries only (culture, parent, tile, farm class, year), so nothing reaching `culture` can distinguish a daughter that hopped from one that walked. The fact is produced and then dropped one struct short of its consumer.

THE REPAIR IS SMALL: a `crossed_water` flag on `culture_spawn`, set where the overseas hop already branches, read in `build_creeds` beside the coastal-cradle and sea-god terms that BL-899 already sums.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING RATHER THAN LEAVING. COLONISATION.md sec Culture arrives by route makes the distribution of pantheons A RECORD OF ROUTES, and a water crossing is the single most consequential thing that can happen to a route. It is also the fact with the best claim of the three to EARN sea legs -- a coastal cradle only says where a people started, a sea god says what they believe, but a crossing says what they actually did. Today the one fact that is a deed rather than a circumstance is the one that is thrown away.

DONE WHEN: a culture whose ancestors crossed water carries that fact into `creed_state`, `sea_legs_q` reads all three terms, and the sweep shows sea legs distributed differently from the two-term derivation.

items.author: Claude (found building BL-898)
items.title: pass_one_handoff has seven red rows because its synthetic fixture no longer produces a war
items.design:
FOUND WHILE BUILDING BL-898, 2026-09-11, and PRE-EXISTING -- that item touched nothing this harness covers.

WHAT IS RED: C5a, C5g, C5h, C5i, C5k, C4b and C6b. The cause is one fact, not seven: the harness strip fixture now produces 2 battles, 2 conquests and ZERO GRUDGE PAIRS, so every row that needs a quarrel to exist has nothing to assert against.

THIS IS A FIXTURE FAILURE, NOT A CODE FAILURE, and the distinction is the whole item. The strip was authored when the sim fought readily on it; the sim has since been reshaped repeatedly -- BL-894 made Settle re-settlement, BL-837 gated reach, BL-896 made ground secede -- and the strip stopped being a world where war happens. The rows are correct and the world under them is wrong.

THE TEMPTING FIX IS THE WRONG ONE. Tuning the strip until a war appears is fitting a fixture to its assertions, and the next sim change breaks it again. The BL-898 agent declined to do it and wrote its own G7 against `era_minus_one_fixture` -- the era generation ACTUALLY RUNS -- instead. That is the pattern worth generalising here.

DONE WHEN: the seven rows either assert against a fixture that genuinely produces a war for a reason that will survive the next sim change, or are re-pointed at the real generated era the way BL-898's G7 is, or are retired with the reason recorded. A harness whose red is permanent and explained is worse than one that is either green or deleted -- it trains everyone to ignore it.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, as lever 3 of BL-823); Claude (split out on closing that umbrella)
items.title: A polity can act on ground it cannot hear from, because there is no communication rung
items.design:
SPLIT OUT OF BL-823 (anti-hegemon levers) ON 2026-09-11, when that umbrella closed. It is the LAST of its six levers still unbuilt; the other five shipped under their own ids.

BEN, 2026-09-08, naming it: before a communication rung is reached, a polity cannot act on ground it cannot HEAR from -- which bounds early growth by GEOGRAPHY rather than by a cap.

IT EARNS ITS PLACE TWICE, which is why it survived the umbrella's closure. It is an anti-hegemon lever, and it is also THE SECOND RUNG OF BEN'S OWN ARC (GENERATION_STRATEGY.md: origin -> COMMUNICATION -> conquest or diplomatic union -> a stable dark age). The arc names four rungs and this is the only one with no mechanism behind it.

IT IS NOT A DUPLICATE OF REACH, AND THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE ITEM. BL-837's reach asks CAN I SUPPLY THIS -- a question about materials moving over terrain. Communication asks CAN I KNOW ABOUT THIS AT ALL -- a question about information, which travels differently, degrades differently, and binds EARLY history where reach binds late. If the build cannot articulate a difference that shows up in the numbers, it is duplicating reach and should be dropped rather than shipped: BL-823's own instruction was to re-read the remaining levers as SUPPORTING reach-gating and to drop any that only duplicate it. That test applies to this item first.

THE CONSTRAINT, unchanged from the umbrella: a lever is a FORCE WITH A VISIBLE CAUSE ON THE MAP, never a term inside an actor and never a penalty that scales with a polity's rank.

DESIGN IS OWED BEFORE BUILD. Open: what the rung IS (a capacity band? a work? a property of the network?); whether it gates the scorer's candidate list or the verb's execution; and how it differs measurably from reach rather than only in prose.

DONE WHEN: a polity demonstrably cannot act on ground it has no communication to; the bound shows up in EARLY history where reach binds late; and the difference from reach is visible in the sweep rather than argued for in a comment.

items.author: Claude (found capture-verifying BL-891)
items.title: The wizard's scripted walk cannot get past round 3, and no script can test whether a human can
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-11 while capture-verifying BL-891 (round 4 arc readout).

THE SYMPTOM. `history_lapse_press.lua` -- the acceptance script that walks the pre-game wizard with REAL presses through ImGui's hit-test -- has four red rows on main. Every Next press after round 3 misses and the wizard stays on round 3 (0-based 2). A purpose-written probe, `scripts/verify/round4_arc_reach.lua`, pressed the column at seven heights from y=995 to y=1070 and none advanced the round.

THE HYPOTHESIS. Round 3 carries a preference block (Drawdown) the pass rounds do not, and BL-891 then added three lines of arc readout above the footer. The footer follows the column's content, so Next appears to have been pushed to or past the bottom edge at 1080p. The capture shows a footer bar clipped at the panel's bottom. A surface that grew until it pushed its own exit off the screen.

TWO THINGS MUST BE SETTLED, AND THE SECOND IS THE MORE IMPORTANT:

1. IS IT ACTUALLY UNREACHABLE FOR A HUMAN? The left column has a scrollbar, so a person may simply scroll down to the footer. If so this is a scripted-walk problem and a minor layout smell. If NOT, the wizard is BLOCKED at round 3 at 1080p and nothing downstream of it can be reached at all -- which would be a release blocker, not a polish item. Needs a live click; Ben was on the PC when this was found.

2. THE VERIFY API CANNOT ASK THE QUESTION. `verify.scroll_panel` resolves only NAMED ledger windows ("tile", "balance", "corporation", "construction", "acquisitions", "generation_ledger") and knows nothing about the wizard's left column. So no script can reach a control that has fallen below that column's fold, and no script can prove one is reachable. That is a hole in the instrument, and it is why this was found by eye rather than by the harness that exists to find it.

ALSO WORTH A LOOK: the verify run reports "window 1720x1080" while captures are 1920x1080. If capture pixels and click coordinates are not the same space, then every coordinate in every wizard press script was read off a capture in the WRONG space, and the ones that pass do so by luck. That would explain why coordinates "read off captures" keep going stale.

DONE WHEN: round 3's Next is reachable and proven so by a script rather than by eye; `verify` can scroll the wizard column; and the capture-versus-click coordinate space is either confirmed identical or documented as not.

items.author: Claude (converged on independently by three agents in the sprint 38 batch)
items.title: BL-837's reach gate -- the phase's primary lever -- refuses zero campaigns in generation's own run
items.design:
FOUND THREE TIMES INDEPENDENTLY ON 2026-09-11, by three agents working different items who had no contact with each other. That convergence is why this is filed at priority A rather than as an observation.

THE READING, STRAIGHT OFF THE SWEEP: `REFUSED reach gate   median 0   (BL-837)`. Across 16 seeds at --epoch 0, in generation's own run, the reach gate refuses NO campaigns at all.

WHY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. BL-823's own resolution note promoted reach-gating from one lever among six to THE PRIMARY LEVER: "an empire persists while its network holds and fragments when it does not, and the number of nations at 1200 CE is a consequence of what got built and stayed maintainable." CIVILISATION.md sec The road is the empire's skeleton is built on the same claim. If the gate refuses nothing, the primary lever is not doing the job the design assigns it -- whatever else is holding the world multipolar, it is not this.

WHAT IT ALREADY BLOCKED, and each was a real cost paid before the cause was known:
  - BL-887 (reach as centre chains) built a correct, cheap centre-relay model and measured NO movement. Tripling the rebate reproduced the default figures EXACTLY. The agent's diagnosis: cheaper reach can only unlock ground a price was keeping shut, and no ground is shut.
  - BL-839 (turbulence lean) leans three forces and two of them are inert. Its reach-cost term is "a toll on a road nobody is stopped on", and its fear term leans a median of 0 candidates. The lean measured as a null result at calm-vs-turbulent on every headline figure.
  - BL-838 (fear of being next) fires in only 6 of 16 worlds and moved hegemony not at all.

SO THE QUESTION IS NOT "TUNE THE GATE". It is WHY nothing reaches it. Candidates worth measuring before changing anything:
  (a) the water-gate legality test (BL-778) refuses a median 969 wet contacts per world and may simply be consuming every candidate the reach gate would otherwise see -- the two gates are in sequence and the first one may be doing all the work;
  (b) the floors are sited where nothing lands, and the recalibration history (250 -> 80 -> 20 on a related floor) suggests this was suspected before;
  (c) the span. The phase runs 400 of its designed 1,600 years, so realms may never get large enough to outrun their own reach.

DO NOT FIX BY RAISING A FLOOR UNTIL THE CAUSE IS KNOWN. Three wrong diagnoses were published in this file's history and every one was caught by one number contradicting another on the same page. The instrument was right every time; the reasoning ahead of it was not.

DONE WHEN: the reason the reach gate refuses nothing is MEASURED and named; and either the gate refuses a non-trivial share of campaigns, or CIVILISATION.md stops calling it the primary lever and says what actually holds the world multipolar.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, two elicitation forms); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Decouple pass 1's stop year from the epoch, so Empires runs its full 1,600 years
items.design:
THE PRECONDITION FOR EVERY READING IN THE CLOSURE CONTRACT. CIVILISATION.md sec The closure of the Empire era states that its readings are taken AT 1200 CE. They cannot be taken at all today.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG. The Empires phase is designed 400 BCE -> 1200 CE (1,600 years) and runs 400 BCE -> 0 CE (400 years). The cause is one coupling: pass 1 stops at the EPOCH, and the game's epoch is 0 CE. BL-871 (empire span) shipped the 400 BCE split and named this gap on screen rather than hiding it -- 'reaching 1200 CE needs an epoch past 0 CE'. That framing is what this item overturns: pass 1's stop year does not need to BE the epoch, it needs to be 1200.

THE SHAPE. Give pass 1 an explicit stop year, defaulting to 1200 CE, independent of the world descriptor's epoch year. stop_after_ancient_era already exists as the halt point (BL-871); what it halts AT is the coupling to remove. Do NOT reach 1200 by moving the epoch to 1960 -- that pulls in Globalisation and Digitisation (BL-913), neither of which is built, and makes this item depend on two phases that do not exist.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE POINT AND MUST NOT BE SOFTENED (Ben, 2026-09-11, told the cost and choosing it anyway). Running 1,600 years instead of 400 will move EVERY number in sprint 38's scoreboard, including the ones already accepted -- hegemony 0/16, largest share median 12%, secessions median 2, the rise/peak/fall count, the materials sink at 8%. Those figures were all read at a quarter span. Re-read them; do not tune anything to preserve them, and do not treat a moved number as a regression. A figure measured over 400 years was never a measurement of this phase.

COST IS A REAL RISK AND IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Pass 1 is already the most expensive pass and this quadruples the empire round. Measure the wall clock before and after on history_span_cost; if it lands badly, the affordability rungs in lore/COLLAPSE.md sec The 4000-year problem are the authority, and a shorter STEP is the admissible lever, never a shorter span.

WATCH THE CAPACITY LADDER. CIVILISATION.md sec Open questions already asks whether the ladder's rungs turn over believably in 1,600 years, having been calibrated over 4,000. This item is what makes that question answerable. MEASURE BEFORE TUNING: report the rung turnover, change no constant.

DONE WHEN: the Empires round runs 400 BCE -> 1200 CE with the epoch unchanged at 0 CE; history_sweep reports the span it actually ran on the face of the report; world_determinism is unchanged; and the sprint-38 figures are RE-READ at full span and recorded beside the old ones.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, two elicitation forms); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Print the closure contract's seven readings from history_sweep, at 1200 CE
items.design:
THE CONTRACT IS A STRUCT PLUS A SCOREBOARD, AND THIS IS THE SCOREBOARD. pass_one_output_valid checks internal consistency -- shares sum to 1000, holdings name living polities, grudges name polities in range. It cannot check SHAPE, and shape is the whole of what the closure requires.

WHY IT EXISTS, stated as plainly as the handoff stated it: four items delivered on 2026-09-11 (BL-887 reach chains, BL-839 turbulence lean, BL-838 fear-of-next, BL-905 reach gate) were each measured honestly and NONE could be JUDGED, because nothing downstream asked for anything specific. A mechanism inside the Empire phase is judged by whether it moves a reading here. Without this surface, sprint 38's pattern repeats by default.

THE SEVEN READINGS are CIVILISATION.md sec What the closure is judged on: explorer set, strength spread, contact, directed wants, markets, inherited network, grudges still biting. Each is read OVER A SEED SPREAD and never per-world.

NO TARGET NUMBERS ARE SET IN THIS ITEM. The spread is measured first and the admissible band is argued from the measurement, exactly as sprint 38's done_when requires and as the opposition-bar question in CIVILISATION.md sec Open questions already insists. A number picked to make one seed look right is the failure mode this item exists to prevent, not a shortcut it may take.

A SEED THAT REFUSES A READING IS LEGITIMATE; A SPREAD THAT REFUSES ONE IS NOT. Assert on the spread. A per-world assertion here would re-introduce the forced outcome the whole phase is designed against.

DEPENDS on BL-906 (empire span to 1200) for the readings to mean anything, and reports partial readings honestly for the fields BL-908/909/910/911/912 have not yet supplied -- a missing field prints as MISSING, never as zero.

DONE WHEN: history_sweep prints all seven readings with the year they were taken; a field whose source is unbuilt says so; and the spread reading for each is recorded in the item's resolution as the baseline every later mechanism is judged against.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, two elicitation forms); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: A directed polity-to-polity contact record, carried across the handoff
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-11, form): CONTACT HOLDS BETWEEN POLITIES, not cultures and not landmasses. CIVILISATION.md sec Contact is polity to polity owns the design.

WHAT IT IS FOR. Without a contact record every region sits in one connected graph, so there is nothing for an exploration age to discover and no way to say that a landmass has never been crossed to. Contact is what makes ignorance a FACT rather than an absence.

THE SHAPE IS THE GRUDGE TABLE'S. pass_one_output::grudges is already a directed, named, event-carrying record between polities and it validates cleanly; contact is the same object with a different cause. Reuse the idiom rather than inventing a second one -- two tables of the same shape with different conventions is how a reader ends up trusting the wrong one.

WHAT IS DISCOVERED IS PEOPLE, NOT EMPTY LAND, and this constrains the item. COLONISATION.md ends the migration when every habitable landmass carries some culture, and CIVILISATION.md sec What the dark age must leave DECLINED ground released back to nobody. So an unmet landmass at 1200 CE is SETTLED AND UNMET. Do not add an 'unclaimed ground' concept; there is none by ruling.

LANDMASS IDENTITY IS DERIVED, NOT STORED (Ben's choice of grain). A landmass question is answered by walking the polity contact graph against region::domain. A second landmass-grain table would be a competing truth with nothing extra in it.

POLITIES DIE AND THAT IS A KNOWN COST OF THIS GRAIN. A polity conquered before 1200 CE takes its contacts with it unless conquest INHERITS them. Decide that explicitly and write it down: the defensible reading is that a conqueror inherits what its victim knew, because the knowledge was in the seat. Raise it rather than defaulting it.

DONE WHEN: contact is recorded as it happens during the phase, crosses in pass_one_output, validates in pass_one_output_valid the way grudges do, and the sweep can report at least one unmet pair on some seeds.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, two elicitation forms); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: A directed want table: A knows B holds what A lacks
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-11): a good you know exists, that you do not have, is a MOTIVE on its own. The want needs no price and this phase still has no market during its span. CIVILISATION.md sec The directed want owns the design.

DIRECTED, NOT A SCARCITY LIST (Ben's explicit choice over the per-polity alternative). A scarcity list says a realm is short of something and names no object for the shortage. The directed form is what makes the exploration age's first act explicable -- THIS realm sailed to THAT one, for THAT -- rather than a roll over a list of absences.

TWO INPUTS. (1) Endowment: what B's ground holds that A's reachable ground does not, off the four region windows (farm/ore/energy/port). (2) What B's MARKET SHOWS (Ben, 2026-09-11) -- the conditions a neighbour's market makes visible, which is the signal a trading age actually acts on. The second input is why BL-910 exists and is why this item requires it.

A WANT REQUIRES CONTACT. The table is defined only over pairs BL-908's record already joins. Without that gate it is omniscience with extra steps, and the exploration age has nothing to discover because every realm already wants everything.

NO PRICE, NO ORDER BOOK, NO DEMAND CURVE. CIVILISATION.md sec Materials are spent when something happens is unchanged. Population demand is the economy pass's and must not leak backwards into a phase with no price -- the want is a KNOWN ABSENCE plus a KNOWN HOLDER, nothing more.

THE MECHANISM TRANSFERS, THE PROPER NOUN DOES NOT. The historical analogy Ben raised is a mechanism reference only (io-standing-rules sec Terms & docs): no Earth name appears in generated content.

DONE WHEN: the want table crosses in pass_one_output, is non-empty on a spread, points ACROSS contact rather than within it, and every entry names both the holder and the thing wanted.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, two elicitation forms); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Capitals exist at the close, and markets stand on them at 1200 CE
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-11): near the end of the Empire pass, ensure capital cities exist, and spawn markets centred on them. That gives the exploration age a market substrate in simplified form without giving this phase a market during its span. CIVILISATION.md sec Capitals exist at the close owns the design.

THIS MOVES A BUILT DESIGN'S TIMING, IT DOES NOT OPEN A NEW ONE, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE ITEM. economy/MARKETS.md sec Market centres and seeding already carries Ben's 2026-09-03 line -- markets should begin to emerge towards the end of this phase -- and the junction-gated carve LANDED (BL-768, roads and markets from history). But it carves at WORLD-GEN, at the epoch, reading the history's corridor record afterwards. The closure needs markets standing AT 1200 CE as an output of this phase. Read the built carve before writing anything: the intent is to re-time and re-anchor it, not to duplicate it.

THE CAPITAL IS THE SEAT THE POLITY ALREADY GOVERNS FROM (CIVILISATION.md sec The unit is the city state -- region::is_seat, seeded one per polity at its capital). A market centre is a PROMOTION of an existing fact, never a new placement pass. Do not introduce a capital id space.

NO QUOTA. A polity that ends the phase without a governable seat has no market. That is the same permission a city state gets and it must not become a floor that manufactures a capital for every surviving realm -- manufacturing one is the forced outcome this project files items to avoid.

A MARKET AT THE CLOSE IS A PLACE AND A VISIBLE CONDITION, NOT AN ORDER BOOK. No firms, no clearing tick, no price band, no inventory -- those are the economy pass's and the no-market ruling for this phase is unchanged. What it carries is enough for a stranger to look at it and want something, which is exactly what BL-909's second input reads.

DONE WHEN: surviving polities with a seat carry a capital at 1200 CE, a market centre stands on each, both cross in pass_one_output, and a polity without a seat carries neither.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, two elicitation forms); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: The surviving road network crosses the handoff, inherited unevenly
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-11, form): the roads cross the handoff, in this contract. CIVILISATION.md sec The network is the estate owns the design.

THE HOLE. CIVILISATION.md sec What the dark age must leave names roads that outlive their builders as one of THREE things the fragments must carry, and pass_one_output carries no network at all. A network that does not cross cannot be inherited by anybody, so output 2 of the dark-age contract is currently unmet by construction rather than by tuning.

THIS IS WHAT MAKES COLLAPSE CONSEQUENTIAL RATHER THAN MERELY TERMINAL. Collapse is network failure (CIVILISATION.md sec How an empire actually falls), so what an empire leaves is precisely the part of its network that still stands. Whoever holds that ground starts the exploration age ahead of whoever does not.

UNEVEN IS THE REQUIREMENT, NOT A SIDE EFFECT. An evenly-inherited network is the flat map GENERATION_STRATEGY.md sec Asymmetry is the deliverable exists to prevent, so the sweep reads the SPREAD of inherited network across fragments, not its total.

RESPECT THE EXISTING SEAM. BL-768's feasibility finding stands and is not re-litigated here: the sim has no write channel to the world and no tile-grain route, so roads are STAMPED FROM its record by a pass afterwards, never laid inside it. What crosses is therefore the sim's own record of what was built and walked -- the works roster's road rows -- not a tile list.

DONE WHEN: the surviving network crosses in pass_one_output, the stamp pass reads it from there rather than from live sim state, and the sweep reports its spread across surviving polities.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, two elicitation forms); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Wire the Empire tree into the sim: the sim reads nodes, and the rim is the explorer threshold
items.design:
THE LARGEST OUTSTANDING PIECE OF GENERATION WORK, AND THE ONE THAT MAKES BEN'S SECOND ASPECT REAL. Three trees are authored and lint-green -- 143 nodes across colonisation_tree.json, empire_tree.json and industry_tree.json -- and NOTHING IN src/ READS ANY OF THEM. (src/world/tech_tree.* is the unrelated CAMPAIGN tree loaded from scripts/tech_tree.lua; do not confuse them.) trees/TREES.md states 'the sim reads nodes, not bands' (Ben, 2026-09-10) and the code reads bands only. This item closes that for the EMPIRE tree; colonisation and industry are out of scope.

SCOPE IS WIRE ONLY -- NO GENERATION RENDER (Ben, 2026-09-11, form + notes): 'the tech tree will be available via the tech ledger later - we don't need to render it in generation, and we don't have a reference to view each polity's tree regardless.' Wiring the tree into the sim and showing it to a player are separate decisions and only the first is taken.

WHY A BAND CANNOT DO THIS JOB. A band is a ladder everyone climbs in the same order, so difference under it is only ever HOW FAR, never WHICH WAY. The closure contract's explorer set is a THRESHOLD CROSSED (Ben, 2026-09-11): a per-polity boolean read off EM-SP-4m, 'The Enforceable Promise', whose sole effect opens the industry tree and whose requires are EM-PE-4a and EM-RD-4b. That is a fact about what a realm BUILT, and no scalar expresses it.

THE FORK IS WHAT MAKES DIFFERENCE INDEPENDENT OF ECONOMIC MIGHT, and it is the half most likely to be dropped as an optimisation. A closed fork side goes dark permanently, so two wealthy realms can end the phase incapable of the same things because they CHOSE differently. Without the fork, technological difference collapses into a restatement of size -- which is the one thing this output must not be. The empire tree carries 1 fork; it is load-bearing.

STATE, per trees/TREES.md sec State: one 64-bit mask per tree plus one accumulated-progress integer for the node being invested in. Research is a FLOW derived from the labour split (a fraction of the industry slice, scaled by spire ring and contact degree), never a resource -- BL-867 (materials spent on action) already splits labour three ways, so the input exists.

WITHIN THE EXISTING GRANT, and this is asserted rather than assumed. Choosing a node is an argument to the Invest verb the register already covers (ai/AI_OPPONENT.md sec 11); it issues no new verb and plans nothing. If the implementation finds itself wanting a verb the register does not name, STOP and raise a new grant -- NR-517 is the precedent for why reading an existing grant as covering a new subject is the exact failure this rule exists to prevent.

DETERMINISM. Node choice is a seeded, scored argmax over a TOTAL order with an explicit tie-break, in fixed node-id order. No float in the decision path; the sim is integer fixed-point.

SUGGESTED SLICING, since this is difficulty 6: (a) tree state + load the store into a Lua-free TU; (b) the Invest verb spends progress on a node instead of a band; (c) the scorer, per TREES.md sec The scorer; (d) the rim reading into pass_one_output. Slice (d) is what BL-907 needs and can land before (c) is good.

DONE WHEN: a polity's empire-tree mask is real state, Invest buys nodes, the rim milestone is readable per polity at 1200 CE and crosses in pass_one_output, world_determinism is unchanged, and the sweep shows SOME surviving realms holding the rim and not all.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, two elicitation forms); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Split pass 2 into Globalisation (1200-1660) and Digitisation (1660-1960), and remove the coast
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-11): 'It's a consequence of splitting exploration and digitisation. The years up to date are: 2400 BCE to 400 BCE for Culture. 400 BCE to 1200 CE for Empires. 1200 CE to 1660 CE for Globalisation. 1660 CE to 1960 CE for Digitisation.'

WHAT THIS SUPERSEDES. Pass 2 was one economy span, 1560 -> 1960, with 1200 -> 1560 a DELIBERATE unsimulated coast (GENERATION_STRATEGY.md sec Pass 2 is the economy pass). Both are now gone: exploration and digitisation are different subjects with different terminating conditions, and the span between 1200 and 1560 is simulated rather than coasted. 1960 and 1200 are unmoved, so pass 1, the epoch and the industrial-band campaign are untouched.

ALREADY RECORDED: the new table is written into CIVILISATION.md sec The closure of the Empire era and GENERATION_STRATEGY.md sec Pass 2, which now carries the supersession. This item is the rest.

DESIGN IS OWED, and that is why this is design-owed rather than designed. Settled: the four spans. NOT settled: what Globalisation's terminating condition is beyond a year; whether it is the same engine with sea legs open or a distinct round; which wizard round each becomes (STARTUP.md names five rounds, ending at Industrialisation, and there are now six phases); whether the Industry tree opens at 1200 or at 1660; and what Digitisation does that Globalisation does not.

THE DOC RECONCILIATION IS PART OF THIS ITEM AND IS NOT SMALL. Sibling docs still assert 1560 -> 1960 and the dark-age coast -- grep the OLD wording, not the new. Ben, 2026-09-11: 'Don't stress too much about contradictions - once we have the full pipeline we will go over it in detail.' So the contradictions are DEFERRED to this item deliberately, not overlooked; that ruling is the licence, and it expires here.

SEQUENCING. Do not start this before the Empire closure is measured. BL-906/907 make the Empire phase readable at 1200 CE, and the closure contract is Globalisation's INPUT -- building the consumer before its input is specified is precisely what the 2026-09-11 redirect stopped.

DONE WHEN: the design questions above are settled on a form, the four spans are consistent across every doc that names one, and the wizard's rounds match the phases.
